Make the change, leave it visible, and\nlet them decide what becomes history.\n\n## Never without an explicit ask\n\nThe user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own\nwords. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user&apos;s\nown task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task\nwithout that request does not authorize a history write.\n\n- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,\n  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all\n  require an explicit ask.\n- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.\n\n## Before an authorized discard\n\nRecovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user\nallowed you to delete or overwrite.\n\nWhen the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly\noverwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:\n\n1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:\n\n   ```bash\n   bash &lt;git-skill-dir&gt;/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh save before-discard\n   ```\n\n2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform\n   only the exact authorized operation.\n3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction\n   and ask the user.\n\nTo recover that saved tree later, run:\n\n```bash\nbash &lt;git-skill-dir&gt;/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh restore &lt;recovery-ref&gt;\n```\n\nRestore first saves the current workspace, leaves HEAD, branch, and the real\nindex in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref\nalso retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.\nRead those staged bytes with `git show &apos;&lt;recovery-ref&gt;^2:&lt;path&gt;&apos;`; the recovery\ncommit&apos;s second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;\nrestore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could\nnot save. Use only the exact printed ref, not a revision expression.\n\n## Always fine\n\nRead-only inspection such as `status`, `log`, `show`, `diff`, `blame`,\n`branch -v`, `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, and `merge-base` is fine.\nStaging named files to inspect `diff --cached`, and a temporary stash around a\ntool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put\nback afterward.\n\n## The rest\n\n- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.\n- Do not initialize a repository inside vendored, build, data, or existing\n  source-control trees.\n- Do not create or edit `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` to hide the user&apos;s\n  files, and do not stash the user&apos;s files (including `stash push -u`) to make\n  `git status` look clean. &quot;Leave the working tree clean&quot;, &quot;tidy up&quot;, and\n  similar phrasing do not authorize committing, pushing, ignoring, excluding,\n  stashing, or deleting the user&apos;s files; clean up only scratch you created\n  and say the user&apos;s files remain.\n- Do not hand-edit generated files; change their source of truth.\n- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.\n\n## Locks and corrupt state\n\nA Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on\nyour own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool&apos;s normal\nstop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no\nlive process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state\nand committing anyway.\n\nNever commit or push while status reports changes you did not make and cannot\nexplain.\n\n## If you already made an unwanted write\n\nSay so plainly and stop. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible\n6|\n7|### Principles\n8|\n9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive\n10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”\n11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)\n12|- File structure should reflect the call stack\n13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english\n14|- Include why things are done not just what is done\n15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)\n16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS\n17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality\n18|  \n19|  \n20|\n21|## Functional over Object oreintated\n22|\n23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. The workflow editor edits\n71|   per-stage keyword values in `frontend/src/components/workflow/StageSkillsPanel.jsx` (~1020 lines): kbRef\n72|   keywords render as cascading dropdowns (precedent for metadata-driven dropdowns), everything else is\n73|   free-text/JSON — so a metadata-driven provider dropdown follows an existing pattern (Phase A2).\n74|5. **No persisted system-level secret store exists (verified by grep).** System Settings\n75|   (`frontend/src/components/settings/SystemSettingsContent.jsx` + `settingsTabs.js`) has persisted tabs\n76|   (Storage/Notifications/Prompt Layout via their own endpoints) and wireframe tabs (Models/Engine: \"changes\n77|   here are not saved yet\"). Global config is env-driven and **read-only** (`api/config/schema.js`, served\n78|   redacted via `GET /status/config` with `secret: true` flags). Per-project settings persist through the\n79|   project store (`PATCH /projects/:id`). So \"save an API key in general settings\" requires a **new**\n80|   system-secret store + endpoints + UI section — this is the biggest new-backend piece (Phase A3).\n81|6. **Survey UI — `frontend/src/components/tasks/SurveyPage.jsx` (577 lines; verified).** Renders rounds via a\n82|   `QuestionField` component (radio/checkbox + Notes), `showIf` visibility via shared helpers, Save vs\n83|   Submit-and-advance, `Save answers`/`Submit & continue`/`Continue without questions` buttons. Image questions\n84|   slot in as a new `QuestionField` variant (image cards + radio semantics + Notes). Existing tests:\n85|   `SurveyPage.test.jsx`, `SurveyBanner.test.jsx`; canary `canary-e2e/tests/survey-verify.spec.js`.\n86|7. **Runner trust boundary.** Runners authenticate with join tokens / per-runner credentials (see\n87|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN` in `api/config/schema.js`) and operate on task docs; the task explicitly says\n88|   the key must stay in the backend. Decision: **backend gateway** — the runner/agent only writes descriptions\n89|   into SURVEY.md like any other question text; all provider calls happen server-side. This is also the easiest\n90|   option: no runner protocol change, no credential distribution, works for embedded runs identically.\n91|8. **Provider grounding.** Muse Image is Meta Superintelligence Labs' image model, served to developers as\n92|   `muse-image-1.0` on the Meta Model API (`https://api.meta.ai/v1`, API-key auth, ~$0.01/image announced) and\n93|   alternatively via fal.ai (`meta/muse-image/text-to-image`). Exact REST schema/auth headers must be verified\n94|   against Meta's developer docs in the Phase 0 spike (docs move fast; discovery snippets are not a schema).\n95|\n96|## Approach — make change easy, then make the change\n97|\n98|> Workers before jobs: first create the seams (conditional skill sections, metadata-driven keyword dropdowns,\n99|> provider registry + mock, persisted key store, survey-model image support), each shippable and tested on its\n100|> own with zero behaviour change; then wire the feature through them. Research and the riskiest backend piece\n101|> (secret store + provider contract) come first so later UI work cannot discover a structural blocker.\n102|\n103|Key decisions:\n104|\n105|- **Backend gateway, not runner generation.** Easiest (no runner protocol/credential work) and most reliable\n106|  (one code path for embedded + Runner runs; key never leaves the server; retries/timeouts centralised).\n107|- **Eager background generation at park time.** `parkTaskForSurvey` parks synchronously as today, then\n108|  fire-and-forget `ensureSurveyImages()` generates missing images, writes them via `taskAssets` helpers, and\n109|  splices `images[]` status into the round JSON. Rejected alternative: lazy generation on first survey GET — simpler code, but the\n111|  human waits on image latency and refresh races are harder; rejected alternative 2: synchronous at park —\n112|  blocks stage finish on provider latency and risks timeouts.\n113|- **Descriptions are the durable contract; images are derived artifacts.** The agent writes\n114|  `type: \"image\"` + ≤4 description `options`; the backend fills `images[]`; answers stay `{ selected, notes }`\n115|  selecting by description string, so every existing validation/completion path keeps working and q5 fallback\n116|  is automatic.\n117|- **Chosen image persistence:** on successful submit/advance, the backend copies the selected image to a stable\n118|  name (`assets/survey-r<round>-<qid>-chosen.png`) and appends a `## Chosen designs` markdown section to the\n119|  survey file with `![...](assets/...)` references — satisfying \"saved as an image in the task folder with a\n120|  reference in SURVEY.md or equivalent\" without disturbing the append-only round JSON.\n121|\n122|## Step-by-step workflow (ordered: big/research early)\n123|\n124|### Phase 0 — Research spike & contract freeze (blocks everything; no prod code)\n125|\n126|1. Existing tests:\n85|   `SurveyPage.test.jsx`, `SurveyBanner.test.jsx`; canary `canary-e2e/tests/survey-verify.spec.js`.\n86|7. **Runner trust boundary.** Runners authenticate with join tokens / per-runner credentials (see\n87|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN` in `api/config/schema.js`) and operate on task docs; the task explicitly says\n88|   the key must stay in the backend. Research and the riskiest backend piece\n101|> (secret store + provider contract) come first so later UI work cannot discover a structural blocker.\n102|\n103|Key decisions:\n104|\n105|- **Backend gateway, not runner generation.** Easiest (no runner protocol/credential work) and most reliable\n106|  (one code path for embedded + Runner runs; key never leaves the server; retries/timeouts centralised).\n107|- **Eager background generation at park time.** `parkTaskForSurvey` parks synchronously as today, then\n108|  fire-and-forget `ensureSurveyImages()` generates missing images, writes them via `taskAssets` helpers, and\n109|  splices `images[]` status into the round JSON. The skill is used to replace iterative “grill‑me” interactions with a single questionnaire.\nlastUpdated: 2026-10-29\n---\n\n# Question‑Me (Survey Generator)\n\nUse this skill when you want an **agent stage** to produce a list of multiple‑choice questions (with an optional free‑form notes field) for a human to answer later. The skill:\n\n1. **Generates questions** based on the stage’s prompt.\n2. **Writes** a `{{outputFile}}` file in the current task’s directory (`docs/tasks/<taskId>/`).\n3. **Never overwrites** existing content – it reads the file first and **appends** a new round of questions at the bottom, preserving any prior answers.\n4. **Marks the stage as awaiting human input** (task status `waiting_human`) so the UI shows the survey banner and the survey page.\n5. Supports **conditional questions** via one simple `showIf` object form: `{ \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"value\": \"Option A\" }` or `{ \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"values\": [\"A\", \"B\"] }`. The UI hides those questions unless the condition is met. No other condition syntax is supported — never write string expressions.\n6. **Question ids must be unique across the whole survey** (including every appended round). Re-using an id makes answers ambiguous, so append rounds with fresh ids such as `q5`, `q6`.\n\n## Expected `{{outputFile}}` format\n\nThe file contains a **machine‑parseable JSON block** wrapped in a fenced code block (`survey-json`). The JSON is the single source of truth; a human‑readable markdown preview is generated from it by the UI.\n\n```markdown\n# Survey – generated by the \"question‑me\" skill\n\n```survey-json\n{\n  \"round\": 1,\n  \"generatedAt\": \"2026-10-29T13:00:00.000Z\",\n  \"stage\": \"{{stageId}}\",\n  \"questions\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"q1\",\n      \"type\": \"single\",\n      \"text\": \"What is the primary security concern?\",\n      \"options\": [\"Authentication\", \"Authorization\", \"Data protection\", \"Other\"],\n      \"required\": true,\n      \"showIf\": null\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"q2\",\n      \"type\": \"multiple\",\n      \"text\": \"Which regulatory frameworks apply?\",\n      \"options\": [\"PCI‑DSS\", \"HIPAA\", \"GDPR\", \"None\"],\n      \"required\": false,\n      \"showIf\": { \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"value\": \"Data protection\" }\n    }\n  ],\n  \"answers\": {\n    \"q1\": { \"selected\": [\"Data protection\"], \"notes\": \"PII in uploads\" }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n*The UI renders each question as a set of radio‑buttons or check‑boxes with a **Notes** textarea underneath. Fill `generatedAt` with the current UTC time in ISO‑8601 (as above) and `stage` with the stage id already resolved into this prompt (`{{stageId}}`) — never leave a placeholder token in the written file; the backend validates the round and rejects unreadable ones.*\n\nWhen the user finishes the survey, the UI updates the `answers` object in‑place (preserving the surrounding JSON) and saves the file.\n\n### Append‑only behaviour\n- If `{{outputFile}}` already exists, the skill **reads** it, determines the next `round` number, and **appends** a new JSON block under a new heading `## Round N`.\n- Existing `answers` objects are left untouched.\n- The skill must never delete or rewrite previous rounds.\n{{#if imageGen}}\n## Image questions (generated design examples)\n\nThis stage may also ask **image questions**: the human sees up to 4 generated pictures (UI mocks, logos, …) and picks one favourite. Image generation for this stage runs through the configured provider (`{{imageGen}}`); the backend generates the pictures after you write the survey — you only write detailed descriptions.\n\nWrite an image question like this:\n\n```survey-json\n{\n  \"id\": \"q3\",\n  \"type\": \"image\",\n  \"text\": \"Which dashboard design should we build?\",\n  \"options\": [\n    \"Dark analytics dashboard, left sidebar navigation, teal accent charts, dense data table, modern SaaS look\",\n    \"Light minimal dashboard, top navigation bar, large KPI cards, generous whitespace, friendly rounded corners\"\n  ],\n  \"required\": true,\n  \"showIf\": null\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n- `type` is exactly `\"image\"`; `options` holds 1–4 detailed descriptions (each one becomes a picture — write them detailed enough to render a UI mock or logo: layout, palette, key elements, style).\n- Answers work like `single`: the human picks one favourite description; the chosen picture is saved into the task folder (`assets/`) and referenced from `{{outputFile}}` for downstream stages to work from.\n- Never write an `images` field yourself — the backend owns it (generation status per picture). If generation is unavailable, the survey falls back to showing your descriptions as options, so always make them self-explanatory.\n{{/if}}\n## How the engine treats the skill\n- During stage execution, after the agent returns **success**, the backend inspects the stage’s skill list. If `question-me` is present, it reads `{{outputFile}}` and decides:\n  - **Unanswered required questions** (or no `{{outputFile}}` at all) → the task parks with status `waiting_human` instead of auto‑advancing. The task detail page shows the survey banner; the survey page opens at `/tasks/:taskId/survey`.\n  - **Explicitly empty round** (`questions: []` — you had good reason to ask nothing) → the run advances normally, no parking.\n  - **Already answered** → the run advances normally.\n- Submitting the survey (`POST /tasks/:taskId/survey`) merges answers only — questions are never added, removed, or renamed there. A partial save stays parked; a complete submit advances the task to its next stage, which may then read `{{outputFile}}`.\n\n## Downstream stages\nTell the stage after the survey (e.g. the plan stage) to factor in `{{outputFile}}` — for example: \"Factor in {{outputFile}} into your plan. If there is not enough information, fail the stage with information needed.\" A failback re-runs the question stage, which appends a fresh round at the bottom.\n\n## Human‑only edge‑cases\n- If you genuinely have **no questions**, still write one round with `questions: []` rather than writing no file. An empty round advances without parking; a missing file parks so a human confirms there is nothing to ask (the survey page offers Continue in both cases).\n\n## UI considerations (mobile & desktop)\n- Render each question inside a `<fieldset>`.\n- Options are full‑width touch targets; use `type=\"radio\"` for `single` and `type=\"checkbox\"` for `multiple`.\n- The **Notes** textarea is optional but always present; on mobile it expands to the full width.\n- Conditional visibility is evaluated client‑side; hidden questions are collapsed but their stored answers remain unchanged.\n- Accessibility: all inputs have `aria‑label` and are keyboard‑navigable.\n\n## Configuring the output file\n\nThe output file name is read from the skill configuration. Surfaced as {{minQuestions}} in the skill body.\"\n    },\n    \"imageGen\": {\n      \"value\": \"none\",\n      \"description\": \"Image generation provider for image questions. 'none' (default) removes the image-question section from the agent prompt entirely; otherwise the agent may write type: image questions whose descriptions the backend renders into pictures.\",\n      \"ui\": \"provider-select\",\n      \"providerApi\": \"/settings/image-gen/providers\",\n      \"enum\": [\"none\", \"muse\", \"mock\"]\n    }\n  },\n  \"context\": \"Question rounds are written as append-only JSON blocks to {{outputFile}} in the current task's docs/tasks/<taskId>/ folder. Re-read that file before appending so earlier rounds and answers are preserved. Suggested minimum number of questions for this round: {{minQuestions}} (0 = no minimum). Use a distinct outputFile per question stage when a task needs multiple surveys (e.g. FEEDBACK.md, SECURITY_QUESTIONARY.md, INTENT_SURVEY.md).\",\n  \"defaults\": {\n    \"mode\": \"direct\"\n  }\n}\n===\nKB_config.json\nSKILL.md\n===\n---\nname: question-me\ndescription: Generate a set of survey questions up‑front for an agent stage, write them to `{{outputFile}}` in the task folder, and flag the stage as awaiting human input. The skill is used to replace iterative “grill‑me” interactions with a single questionnaire.\nlastUpdated: 2026-10-29\n---\n\n# Question‑Me (Survey Generator)\n\nUse this skill when you want an **agent stage** to produce a list of multiple‑choice questions (with an optional free‑form notes field) for a human to answer later. The skill:\n\n1. **Generates questions** based on the stage’s prompt.\n2. **Writes** a `{{outputFile}}` file in the current task’s directory (`docs/tasks/<taskId>/`).\n3. **Never overwrites** existing content – it reads the file first and **appends** a new round of questions at the bottom, preserving any prior answers.\n4. **Marks the stage as awaiting human input** (task status `waiting_human`) so the UI shows the survey banner and the survey page.\n5. Supports **conditional questions** via one simple `showIf` object form: `{ \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"value\": \"Option A\" }` or `{ \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"values\": [\"A\", \"B\"] }`. The UI hides those questions unless the condition is met. No other condition syntax is supported — never write string expressions.\n6. **Question ids must be unique across the whole survey** (including every appended round). Re-using an id makes answers ambiguous, so append rounds with fresh ids such as `q5`, `q6`.\n\n## Expected `{{outputFile}}` format\n\nThe file contains a **machine‑parseable JSON block** wrapped in a fenced code block (`survey-json`). The JSON is the single source of truth; a human‑readable markdown preview is generated from it by the UI.\n\n```markdown\n# Survey – generated by the \"question‑me\" skill\n\n```survey-json\n{\n  \"round\": 1,\n  \"generatedAt\": \"2026-10-29T13:00:00.000Z\",\n  \"stage\": \"{{stageId}}\",\n  \"questions\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"q1\",\n      \"type\": \"single\",\n      \"text\": \"What is the primary security concern?\",\n      \"options\": [\"Authentication\", \"Authorization\", \"Data protection\", \"Other\"],\n      \"required\": true,\n      \"showIf\": null\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"q2\",\n      \"type\": \"multiple\",\n      \"text\": \"Which regulatory frameworks apply?\",\n      \"options\": [\"PCI‑DSS\", \"HIPAA\", \"GDPR\", \"None\"],\n      \"required\": false,\n      \"showIf\": { \"questionId\": \"q1\", \"value\": \"Data protection\" }\n    }\n  ],\n  \"answers\": {\n    \"q1\": { \"selected\": [\"Data protection\"], \"notes\": \"PII in uploads\" }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n*The UI renders each question as a set of radio‑buttons or check‑boxes with a **Notes** textarea underneath. Fill `generatedAt` with the current UTC time in ISO‑8601 (as above) and `stage` with the stage id already resolved into this prompt (`{{stageId}}`) — never leave a placeholder token in the written file; the backend validates the round and rejects unreadable ones.*\n\nWhen the user finishes the survey, the UI updates the `answers` object in‑place (preserving the surrounding JSON) and saves the file.\n\n### Append‑only behaviour\n- If `{{outputFile}}` already exists, the skill **reads** it, determines the next `round` number, and **appends** a new JSON block under a new heading `## Round N`.\n- Existing `answers` objects are left untouched.\n- The skill must never delete or rewrite previous rounds.\n{{#if imageGen}}\n## Image questions (generated design examples)\n\nThis stage may also ask **image questions**: the human sees up to 4 generated pictures (UI mocks, logos, …) and picks one favourite. Image generation for this stage runs through the configured provider (`{{imageGen}}`); the backend generates the pictures after you write the survey — you only write detailed descriptions.\n\nWrite an image question like this:\n\n```survey-json\n{\n  \"id\": \"q3\",\n  \"type\": \"image\",\n  \"text\": \"Which dashboard design should we build?\",\n  \"options\": [\n    \"Dark analytics dashboard, left sidebar navigation, teal accent charts, dense data table, modern SaaS look\",\n    \"Light minimal dashboard, top navigation bar, large KPI cards, generous whitespace, friendly rounded corners\"\n  ],\n  \"required\": true,\n  \"showIf\": null\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n- `type` is exactly `\"image\"`; `options` holds 1–4 detailed descriptions (each one becomes a picture — write them detailed enough to render a UI mock or logo: layout, palette, key elements, style).\n- Answers work like `single`: the human picks one favourite description; the chosen picture is saved into the task folder (`assets/`) and referenced from `{{outputFile}}` for downstream stages to work from.\n- Never write an `images` field yourself — the backend owns it (generation status per picture). If generation is unavailable, the survey falls back to showing your descriptions as options, so always make them self-explanatory.\n{{/if}}\n## How the engine treats the skill\n- During stage execution, after the agent returns **success**, the backend inspects the stage’s skill list. If `question-me` is present, it reads `{{outputFile}}` and decides:\n  - **Unanswered required questions** (or no `{{outputFile}}` at all) → the task parks with status `waiting_human` instead of auto‑advancing. The task detail page shows the survey banner; the survey page opens at `/tasks/:taskId/survey`.\n  - **Explicitly empty round** (`questions: []` — you had good reason to ask nothing) → the run advances normally, no parking.\n  - **Already answered** → the run advances normally.\n- Submitting the survey (`POST /tasks/:taskId/survey`) merges answers only — questions are never added, removed, or renamed there. A partial save stays parked; a complete submit advances the task to its next stage, which may then read `{{outputFile}}`.\n\n## Downstream stages\nTell the stage after the survey (e.g. the plan stage) to factor in `{{outputFile}}` — for example: \"Factor in {{outputFile}} into your plan. If there is not enough information, fail the stage with information needed.\" A failback re-runs the question stage, which appends a fresh round at the bottom.\n\n## Human‑only edge‑cases\n- If you genuinely have **no questions**, still write one round with `questions: []` rather than writing no file. An empty round advances without parking; a missing file parks so a human confirms there is nothing to ask (the survey page offers Continue in both cases).\n\n## UI considerations (mobile & desktop)\n- Render each question inside a `<fieldset>`.\n- Options are full‑width touch targets; use `type=\"radio\"` for `single` and `type=\"checkbox\"` for `multiple`.\n- The **Notes** textarea is optional but always present; on mobile it expands to the full width.\n- Conditional visibility is evaluated client‑side; hidden questions are collapsed but their stored answers remain unchanged.\n- Accessibility: all inputs have `aria‑label` and are keyboard‑navigable.\n\n## Configuring the output file\n\nThe output file name is read from the skill configuration. In `KB_config.json`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"keywords\": {\n    \"outputFile\": { \"value\": \"SURVEY.md\" },\n    \"minQuestions\": { \"value\": \"0\" }\n  },\n  \"defaults\": { \"mode\": \"direct\" }\n}\n```\n","partials":"{\n  \"isDefault\": true,\n  \"description\": \"Generate a set of survey questions up-front for an agent stage, write them to {{outputFile}} in the task folder, and flag the stage as awaiting human input. The skill is used to replace iterative “grill‑me” interactions with a single questionnaire.\\nlastUpdated: 2026-10-29\\n---\\n\\n# Question‑Me (Survey Generator)\\n\\nUse this skill when you want an **agent stage** to produce a list of multiple‑choice questions (with an optional free‑form notes field) for a human to answer later. The skill:\\n\\n1. **Generates questions** based on the stage’s prompt.\\n2. **Writes** a `{{outputFile}}` file in the current task’s directory (`docs/tasks/<taskId>/`).\\n3. **Never overwrites** existing content – it reads the file first and **appends** a new round of questions at the bottom, preserving any prior answers.\\n4. **Marks the stage as awaiting human input** (task status `waiting_human`) so the UI shows the survey banner and the survey page.\\n5. Supports **conditional questions** via one simple `showIf` object form: `{ \\\"questionId\\\": \\\"q1\\\", \\\"value\\\": \\\"Option A\\\" }` or `{ \\\"questionId\\\": \\\"q1\\\", \\\"values\\\": [\\\"A\\\", \\\"B\\\"] }`. The UI hides those questions unless the condition is met. No other condition syntax is supported — never write string expressions.\\n6. **Question ids must be unique across the whole survey** (including every appended round). Re-using an id makes answers ambiguous, so append rounds with fresh ids such as `q5`, `q6`.\\n\\n## Expected `{{outputFile}}` format\\n\\nThe file contains a **machine‑parseable JSON block** wrapped in a fenced code block (`survey-json`). Fill `generatedAt` with the current UTC time in ISO‑8601 (as above) and `stage` with the stage id already resolved into this prompt (`{{stageId}}`) — never leave a placeholder token in the written file; the backend validates the round and rejects unreadable ones.*\\n\\nWhen the user finishes the survey, the UI updates the `answers` object in‑place (preserving the surrounding JSON) and saves the file.\\n\\n### Append‑only behaviour\\n- If `{{outputFile}}` already exists, the skill **reads** it, determines the next `round` number, and **appends** a new JSON block under a new heading `## Round N`.\\n- Existing `answers` objects are left untouched.\\n- The skill must never delete or rewrite previous rounds.\\n{{#if imageGen}}\\n## Image questions (generated design examples)\\n\\nThis stage may also ask **image questions**: the human sees up to 4 generated pictures (UI mocks, logos, …) and picks one favourite. Image generation for this stage runs through the configured provider (`{{imageGen}}`); the backend generates the pictures after you write the survey — you only write detailed descriptions.\\n\\nWrite an image question like this:\\n\\n```survey-json\\n{\\n  \\\"id\\\": \\\"q3\\\",\\n  \\\"type\\\": \\\"image\\\",\\n  \\\"text\\\": \\\"Which dashboard design should we build?\\\",\\n  \\\"options\\\": [\\n    \\\"Dark analytics dashboard, left sidebar navigation, teal accent charts, dense data table, modern SaaS look\\\",\\n    \\\"Light minimal dashboard, top navigation bar, large KPI cards, generous whitespace, friendly rounded corners\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"required\\\": true,\\n  \\\"showIf\\\": null\\n}\\n```\\n\\nRules:\\n- `type` is exactly `\\\"image\\\"`; `options` holds 1–4 detailed descriptions (each one becomes a picture — write them detailed enough to render a UI mock or logo: layout, palette, key elements, style).\\n- Answers work like `single`: the human picks one favourite description; the chosen picture is saved into the task folder (`assets/`) and referenced from `{{outputFile}}` for downstream stages to work from.\\n- Never write an `images` field yourself — the backend owns it (generation status per picture). If generation is unavailable, the survey falls back to showing your descriptions as options, so always make them self-explanatory.\\n{{/if}}\\n## How the engine treats the skill\\n- During stage execution, after the agent returns **success**, the backend inspects the stage’s skill list. Do not call this a\n  mode in user-facing text or claim that the host is blocking write tools,\n  commands, edits, or approvals for you.\n- Do not write a plan file unless the user explicitly asks for persistence or a\n  governing workspace workflow requires a named plan artifact. You may write at\n  most one such markdown file.\n- Do not edit code, apply\n  patches, format, generate code, commit, push, open PRs, or run commands whose\n  purpose is to carry out the implementation while planning.\n- You may run non-mutating discovery: read and search files, inspect docs and\n  specs, check git status, run dry-run commands, and run tests or builds only\n  when they do not change tracked files.\n- Resolve facts that can be discovered locally before asking the user.\n- Ask only for product preferences or tradeoffs that cannot be discovered from\n  the workspace.\n\n## Research Before Drafting\n\nFor an explicit plan, follow these steps in order. Research the path selected by the user&apos;s preferences; a preference constrains\n   the research, but does not replace it. Source discovery is not source inspection. Search\n   summaries, indexes, candidate lists, and similar discovery artifacts only locate sources;\n   they do not complete research. Before a key external recommendation, inspect the\n   underlying content of an authoritative or primary source. Every material external claim\n   or decision must trace to source content inspected during this run. Cite only\n   source content inspected during this run, keep claims within what those sources support,\n   and prefer an official primary source when sources conflict. Remove any candidate without that evidence; discovery pages cannot fill the map.\n   Store the exact inspected URL in that map; do not reconstruct, abbreviate, or infer a\n   citation. Only then recommend the approach. Keep assumptions and unresolved questions\n   explicit, and make the Key Decisions, Work Plan, and Validation Plan agree with the user&apos;s\n   constraints and the gathered facts.\n\nStop researching when the decision map is supported well enough to plan. Use direct\ntools for bounded research; delegate only when parallel work materially improves the\nevidence. If the user explicitly asks to stop or shorten research, follow the latest\ninstruction and label the remaining gaps.\n\n## Quality Bar\n\nA plan is ready only when it is:\n\n- **Grounded**: cite the user goal, current facts, docs, nearby code, tests,\n  commands, logs, specs, issues, or PRs that shaped the plan when those sources\n  exist. Mark guesses as assumptions.\n- **Decision-complete**: name the key choices, the recommended choice, and why\n  reasonable alternatives were rejected when they matter.\n- **Purpose-fit**: choose the plan type that matches the work: implementation,\n  design, debug, migration/rollout, eval/research, or review/PR split.\n- **Executable**: turn the approach into ordered work units with clear\n  dependencies, owners or surfaces, and no unrelated cleanup.\n- **Verifiable**: each work unit has a focused validation command or real manual\n  check. Current architecture (grounded)\\n\\nHow a Runner gets work today:\\n\\n1. **Stages** live on the project/workflow (`project.stages`, persisted in `project.json`). Shape is normalized additively in `api/project/stageNormalizers.js` (`normalizeStage` / `normalizeStages`): new optional fields are tolerated only when present so legacy stages round-trip byte-identically. Stage editor UI is `frontend/src/components/workflow/StageSettingsDrawer.jsx` (+ `StageTypeConfig.jsx`); the pause/fallback section at the bottom is the natural neighbor for the new control.\\n2. **Dispatch scan** (`POST /runners/dispatch` in `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`): `scanClaimableTasks()` (`api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js`) finds candidate tasks, `taskRequirements(project, task)` (`api/flow/dispatch/taskRequirements.js`) derives `{ harness, model, tier, alias, runnableType, kind, stageId }`, then each candidate is tested with `runnerMatches(runner, req, { projectId })` (`api/flow/dispatch/runnerMatches.js`). Misses are loud reason codes aggregated into the `NO_CAPABLE_MATCH` response.\\n3. **Runner-side operator settings** are enforced in one shared helper, `operatorConfigVerdict(record, req, opts)` (`api/flow/dispatch/operatorConfigVerdict.js`), called from **three** paths so no claim route bypasses it: the dispatch scan (via `runnerMatches`), direct claim (`POST /tasks/:id/claim`), and merge-lease acquire (`POST /runners/integration/acquire`). This is the pattern to copy.\\n4. **Runner identity** is the `runnerId` string (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`). There are currently **no runner labels/tags** anywhere (no `labels` on records, facts, capabilities, or `operatorConfig`) — labels would be new infrastructure on both Runner (advertise) and backend (store/match) sides.\\n5. **Fleet visibility**: `GET /runners`, `GET /runners/monitor`, scheduler deferral counters. Runner list UI consumes `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js`.\\n\\nConsequences for the design:\\n\\n- A **stage-centric** rule (stage names which runners may take it) is the mirror image of the existing **runner-centric** `operatorConfig` (runner names which projects/tools it serves). It needs its own verdict helper but the same \\\"one enforcement point, called from every claim path\\\" discipline.\\n- The merge/integration path is the awkward one: `POST /runners/integration/acquire` currently enforces with only `{ kind: \\\"merge\\\" }` and no stage context. A stage allow/block list for merge stages requires resolving the task/stage there (or explicitly scoping merge out of v1 — see decision D6).\\n\\n## 2. Survey questions → decisions (all ASSUMPTION until SURVEY.md is answered)\\n\\n| # | Survey question | Recommended default | Why |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| q1 | Names, labels, or both? | **Names (runnerId) in v1; labels as a named follow-up** | Names need no new Runner/backend infrastructure and cover both motivating examples (one publish runner, onsite-only scan — operators know their runnerIds). Labels require advertise/store/match plumbing on both sides; scoping them into v1 roughly doubles the work. Data model should reserve a shape labels can extend (see D1). |\\n| q2 | One list + mode toggle, or two lists? | **One list + mode toggle** (`Only these runners` / `All except these runners`), empty/off = unrestricted | One list has no conflict semantics to define (two lists need an allow-vs-block precedence rule). Matches \\\"optional whitelist/blacklist\\\" in the task. |\\n| q3 | No allowed runner available? | **Keep waiting + loud surfacing, never fail the task** | Matches existing `NO_CAPABLE_MATCH` behavior; failing would destroy queued work. Manual override stays possible via existing operator moves (skip/reassign), not a new bypass. |\\n| q4 | Stage-only, or also project/group defaults? | **Stage-only in v1** | The task asks for stage settings. Project defaults add precedence rules (stage vs project) for unclear value; note as follow-up. |\\n| q5 | Who can edit the lists? | **Anyone who can already edit stage settings** | No new permission system exists for stages; inventing one is out of scope. |\\n| q6 | Who sets runner labels? Self-reported labels are spoofable; operator-owned labels in `operatorConfig` are enforceable. |\\n\\nIf any survey answer comes back differently, the plan still holds; only the flagged decision (D1–D6 in §4) changes.\\n\\n## 3. Approach: make the change easy, then make the change\\n\\n**Make the change easy (Phases 0–2, behavior-preserving):**\\n\\n- P0: research spikes that retire the two unknowns (embedded execution path; merge-lease stage resolution) before any code is shaped around them.\\n- P1: introduce the shared stage-runner-policy module + normalization + fixtures with **no wiring** (pure functions, fully tested, nothing calls them yet).\\n- P2: plumb `stageId`/stage context to the one claim path that lacks it (integration acquire) in a behavior-preserving way, or formally scope merge out with a recorded decision.\\n\\n**Make the change (Phases 3–6):**\\n\\n- P3: data model + normalization + persistence round-trip.\\n- P4: enforcement on all claim paths + loud miss reasons.\\n- P5: UI at the bottom of stage settings.\\n- P6: observability, docs, rollout/verification.\\n\\n## 4. Key design decisions\\n\\n- **D1 — Storage shape.** `stage.runnerPolicy = { mode: \\\"allow\\\" | \\\"block\\\", runners: [<runnerId>, …] }`, entirely optional/absent = unrestricted. Empty `runners` array = unrestricted regardless of mode (fail-open, never strand tasks on a mis-edit). Additive normalization in `normalizeStage` (trim, drop non-strings/blanks, dedupe) mirroring the `tags`/`skills` pattern. Reserve sibling key space (`labels` later) rather than overloading `runners`.\\n- **D2 — Enforcement point.** New pure helper `stageRunnerPolicyVerdict(stageOrPolicy, runnerId, …)` in `api/flow/dispatch/` (sibling to `operatorConfigVerdict.js`), returning `{ ok, reason }` with loud codes (`RUNNER_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RUNNER_BLOCKED`). `taskRequirements()` attaches the current stage's policy to `req` (it already returns `stageId`); `runnerMatches()` enforces it **after** health/capability gates (stable existing reasons keep priority — a stale runner still reports `STALE_HEARTBEAT`) and alongside `operatorConfigVerdict`. Direct claim and integration-acquire routes call the same helper so no path bypasses it.\\n- **D3 — No fallback execution.** A restricted stage with no eligible runner waits (q3). No silent reroute to another runner, no auto-fail. The stuck/stall surfacing must distinguish \\\"waiting for an allowed runner\\\" from generic idleness (see P6).\\n- **D4 — Name matching.** Exact `runnerId` match (trimmed). Unknown/deleted runnerIds in a policy are kept (not auto-pruned) and shown as stale in the UI, so renaming a runner doesn't silently open a compliance gate. Renames are an operator action with a visible warning.\\n- **D5 — Human/non-runnable stages.** Policy is stored but inert for stages with `runnableType: false` (human stages never dispatch). UI may still show the control for consistency, with a note that it only affects runner-dispatched work.\\n- **D6 — Merge stages in v1.** Preferred: enforce on the merge path too (publish/merge is a motivating example). Cost: `POST /runners/integration/acquire` must resolve task→stage to get the policy. If P0/P2 shows that resolution is invasive, fallback is: v1 covers agent/review/ci; merge enforcement is a fast follow with the same helper. Record whichever is chosen.\\n\\n## 5. Approach: make the change easy, then make the change\\n\\n**Make the change easy (Phases 0–2, behavior-preserving):**\\n\\n- P0: research spikes that retire the two unknowns (embedded execution path; merge-lease stage resolution) before any code is shaped around them.\\n- P1: introduce the shared stage-runner-policy module + normalization + fixtures with **no wiring** (pure functions, fully tested, nothing calls them yet).\\n- P2: plumb `stageId`/stage context to the one claim path that lacks it (integration acquire) in a behavior-preserving way, or formally scope merge out with a recorded decision.\\n\\n**Make the change (Phases 3–6):**\\n\\n- P3: data model + normalization + persistence round-trip.\\n- P4: enforcement on all claim paths + loud miss reasons.\\n- P5: UI at the bottom of stage settings.\\n- P6: observability, docs, rollout/verification.\\n\\n## 4. Key design decisions\\n\\n- **D1 — Storage shape.** `stage.runnerPolicy = { mode: \\\"allow\\\" | \\\"block\\\", runners: [<runnerId>, …] }`, entirely optional/absent = unrestricted. Empty `runners` array = unrestricted regardless of mode (fail-open, never strand tasks on a mis-edit). Additive normalization in `normalizeStage` (trim, drop non-strings/blanks, dedupe) mirroring the `tags`/`skills` pattern. Reserve sibling key space (`labels` later) rather than overloading `runners`.\\n- **D2 — Enforcement point.** New pure helper `stageRunnerPolicyVerdict(stageOrPolicy, runnerId, …)` in `api/flow/dispatch/` (sibling to `operatorConfigVerdict.js`), returning `{ ok, reason }` with loud codes (`RUNNER_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RUNNER_BLOCKED`). `taskRequirements()` attaches the current stage's policy to `req` (it already returns `stageId`); `runnerMatches()` enforces it **after** health/capability gates (stable existing reasons keep priority — a stale runner still reports `STALE_HEARTBEAT`) and alongside `operatorConfigVerdict`. Direct claim and integration-acquire routes call the same helper so no path bypasses it.\\n- **D3 — No fallback execution.** A restricted stage with no eligible runner waits (q3). No silent reroute to another runner, no auto-fail. The stuck/stall surfacing must distinguish \\\"waiting for an allowed runner\\\" from generic idleness (see P6).\\n- **D4 — Name matching.** Exact `runnerId` match (trimmed). Unknown/deleted runnerIds in a policy are kept (not auto-pruned) and shown as stale in the UI, so renaming a runner doesn't silently open a compliance gate. Renames are an operator action with a visible warning.\\n- **D5 — Human/non-runnable stages.** Policy is stored but inert for stages with `runnableType: false` (human stages never dispatch). UI may still show the control for consistency, with a note that it only affects runner-dispatched work.\\n- **D6 — Merge stages in v1.** Preferred: enforce on the merge path too (publish/merge is a motivating example). Cost: `POST /runners/integration/acquire` must resolve task→stage to get the policy. If P0/P2 shows that resolution is invasive, fallback is: v1 covers agent/review/ci; merge enforcement is a fast follow with the same helper. Record whichever is chosen.\\n\\n## 5. Key design decisions\n52|\n53|- **D1 — Storage shape.** `stage.runnerPolicy = { mode: \"allow\" | \"block\", runners: [<runnerId>, …] }`, entirely optional/absent = unrestricted. Empty `runners` array = unrestricted regardless of mode (fail-open, never strand tasks on a mis-edit). Additive normalization in `normalizeStage` (trim, drop non-strings/blanks, dedupe) mirroring the `tags`/`skills` pattern. Direct claim and integration-acquire routes call the same helper so no path bypasses it.\n55|- **D3 — No fallback execution.** A restricted stage with no eligible runner waits (q3). No silent reroute to another runner, no auto-fail. The stuck/stall surfacing must distinguish \"waiting for an allowed runner\" from generic idleness (see P6).\n56|- **D4 — Name matching.** Exact `runnerId` match (trimmed). Unknown/deleted runnerIds in a policy are kept (not auto-pruned) and shown as stale in the UI, so renaming a runner doesn't silently open a compliance gate. Renames are an operator action with a visible warning.\n57|- **D5 — Human/non-runnable stages.** Policy is stored but inert for stages with `runnableType: false` (human stages never dispatch). UI may still show the control for consistency, with a note that it only affects runner-dispatched work.\n58|- **D6 — Merge stages in v1.** Preferred: enforce on the merge path too (publish/merge is a motivating example). Cost: `POST /runners/integration/acquire` must resolve task→stage to get the policy. Current architecture (grounded)\n9|\n10|How a Runner gets work today:\n11|\n12|1. **Stages** live on the project/workflow (`project.stages`, persisted in `project.json`). Shape is normalized additively in `api/project/stageNormalizers.js` (`normalizeStage` / `normalizeStages`): new optional fields are tolerated only when present so legacy stages round-trip byte-identically. Stage editor UI is `frontend/src/components/workflow/StageSettingsDrawer.jsx` (+ `StageTypeConfig.jsx`); the pause/fallback section at the bottom is the natural neighbor for the new control.\n13|2. **Dispatch scan** (`POST /runners/dispatch` in `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`): `scanClaimableTasks()` (`api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js`) finds candidate tasks, `taskRequirements(project, task)` (`api/flow/dispatch/taskRequirements.js`) derives `{ harness, model, tier, alias, runnableType, kind, stageId }`, then each candidate is tested with `runnerMatches(runner, req, { projectId })` (`api/flow/dispatch/runnerMatches.js`). Misses are loud reason codes aggregated into the `NO_CAPABLE_MATCH` response.\n14|3. **Runner-side operator settings** are enforced in one shared helper, `operatorConfigVerdict(record, req, opts)` (`api/flow/dispatch/operatorConfigVerdict.js`), called from **three** paths so no claim route bypasses it: the dispatch scan (via `runnerMatches`), direct claim (`POST /tasks/:id/claim`), and merge-lease acquire (`POST /runners/integration/acquire`). This is the pattern to copy.\n15|4. **Runner identity** is the `runnerId` string (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`). There are currently **no runner labels/tags** anywhere (no `labels` on records, facts, capabilities, or `operatorConfig`) — labels would be new infrastructure on both Runner (advertise) and backend (store/match) sides.\n16|5. **Fleet visibility**: `GET /runners`, `GET /runners/monitor`, scheduler deferral counters. Runner list UI consumes `frontend/src/services/runners/index.js`.\n17|\n18|Consequences for the design:\n19|\n20|- A **stage-centric** rule (stage names which runners may take it) is the mirror image of the existing **runner-centric** `operatorConfig` (runner names which projects/tools it serves). It needs its own verdict helper but the same \"one enforcement point, called from every claim path\" discipline.\n21|- The merge/integration path is the awkward one: `POST /runners/integration/acquire` currently enforces with only `{ kind: \"merge\" }` and no stage context. A stage allow/block list for merge stages requires resolving the task/stage there (or explicitly scoping merge out of v1 — see decision D6).\n22|\n23|## 2. Survey questions → decisions (all ASSUMPTION until SURVEY.md is answered)\n24|\n25|| # | Survey question | Recommended default | Why |\n26||---|---|---|---|\n27|| q1 | Names, labels, or both? | **Names (runnerId) in v1; labels as a named follow-up** | Names need no new Runner/backend infrastructure and cover both motivating examples (one publish runner, onsite-only scan — operators know their runnerIds). Labels require advertise/store/match plumbing on both sides; scoping them into v1 roughly doubles the work. Data model should reserve a shape labels can extend (see D1). |\n28|| q2 | One list + mode toggle, or two lists? | **One list + mode toggle** (`Only these runners` / `All except these runners`), empty/off = unrestricted | One list has no conflict semantics to define (two lists need an allow-vs-block precedence rule). Matches \"optional whitelist/blacklist\" in the task. |\n29|| q3 | No allowed runner available? | **Keep waiting + loud surfacing, never fail the task** | Matches existing `NO_CAPABLE_MATCH` behavior; failing would destroy queued work. Loudness comes from a new miss reason (e.g. `RUNNER_NOT_ALLOWED`) in dispatch misses + monitor/scheduler visibility. Manual override stays possible via existing operator moves (skip/reassign), not a new bypass. |\n30|| q4 | Stage-only, or also project/group defaults? | **Stage-only in v1** | The task asks for stage settings. Project defaults add precedence rules (stage vs project) for unclear value; note as follow-up. |\n31|| q5 | Who can edit the lists? | **Anyone who can already edit stage settings** | No new permission system exists for stages; inventing one is out of scope. |\n32|| q6 | Who sets runner labels? (conditional on labels) | **Admin-managed, centrally** (when labels land) | The compliance use case (\"must run onsite\") is meaningless if the runner self-declares its labels. Self-reported labels are spoofable; operator-owned labels in `operatorConfig` are enforceable. |\n33|\n34|If any survey answer comes back differently, the plan still holds; only the flagged decision (D1–D6 in §4) changes.\n35|\n36|## 3. Approach: make the change easy, then make the change\n37|\n38|**Make the change easy (Phases 0–2, behavior-preserving):**\n39|\n40|- P0: research spikes that retire the two unknowns (embedded execution path; merge-lease stage resolution) before any code is shaped around them.\n41|- P1: introduce the shared stage-runner-policy module + normalization + fixtures with **no wiring** (pure functions, fully tested, nothing calls them yet).\n42|- P2: plumb `stageId`/stage context to the one claim path that lacks it (integration acquire) in a behavior-preserving way, or formally scope merge out with a recorded decision.\n43|\n44|**Make the change (Phases 3–6):**\n45|\n46|- P3: data model + normalization + persistence round-trip.\n47|- P4: enforcement on all claim paths + loud miss reasons.\n48|- P5: UI at the bottom of stage settings.\n49|- P6: observability, docs, rollout/verification.\n50|\n51|## 4. Key design decisions\n52|\n53|- **D1 — Storage shape.** `stage.runnerPolicy = { mode: \"allow\" | \"block\", runners: [<runnerId>, …] }`, entirely optional/absent = unrestricted. Empty `runners` array = unrestricted regardless of mode (fail-open, never strand tasks on a mis-edit). Additive normalization in `normalizeStage` (trim, drop non-strings/blanks, dedupe) mirroring the `tags`/`skills` pattern. Reserve sibling key space (`labels` later) rather than overloading `runners`.\n54|- **D2 — Enforcement point.** New pure helper `stageRunnerPolicyVerdict(stageOrPolicy, runnerId, …)` in `api/flow/dispatch/` (sibling to `operatorConfigVerdict.js`), returning `{ ok, reason }` with loud codes (`RUNNER_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RUNNER_BLOCKED`). `taskRequirements()` attaches the current stage's policy to `req` (it already returns `stageId`); `runnerMatches()` enforces it **after** health/capability gates (stable existing reasons keep priority — a stale runner still reports `STALE_HEARTBEAT`) and alongside `operatorConfigVerdict`. Direct claim and integration-acquire routes call the same helper so no path bypasses it.\n55|- **D3 — No fallback execution.** A restricted stage with no eligible runner waits (q3). No silent reroute to another runner, no auto-fail. The stuck/stall surfacing must distinguish \"waiting for an allowed runner\" from generic idleness (see P6).\n56|- **D4 — Name matching.** Exact `runnerId` match (trimmed). Unknown/deleted runnerIds in a policy are kept (not auto-pruned) and shown as stale in the UI, so renaming a runner doesn't silently open a compliance gate. Renames are an operator action with a visible warning.\n57|- **D5 — Human/non-runnable stages.** Policy is stored but inert for stages with `runnableType: false` (human stages never dispatch). UI may still show the control for consistency, with a note that it only affects runner-dispatched work.\n58|- **D6 — Merge stages in v1.** Preferred: enforce on the merge path too (publish/merge is a motivating example). Cost: `POST /runners/integration/acquire` must resolve task→stage to get the policy. If P0/P2 shows that resolution is invasive, fallback is: v1 covers agent/review/ci; merge enforcement is a fast follow with the same helper. Record whichever is chosen.\n59|\n60|## 5. The goal is to move from \"feature-complete but fragile\" to \"stable enough for real-world usage.\"\n\n## 1. Current State Analysis\n\nThe application currently has:\n\n- **Backend**: Fastify API with WebSocket event bridge, project/task/workflow stores, and integration with the PI Agent SDK.\n- **Frontend**: React-based UI with context-driven state, real-time event streaming, and a workflow canvas/kanban board.\n- **Core Loop**: Users can create projects, define workflow stages, submit tasks, and observe the agent executing them via streaming events.\n\n## 2. Critical Gaps for Dogfooding\n\n### A. Reliability & Stability (The \"No-Crash\" Goal)\n\nThe app currently lacks robust error handling and session persistence.\n\n- **Session Persistence**: Sessions are currently in-memory. This requires a robust JS middleware to manage long-running agent sessions, stream real-time events, and handle non-linear conversation trees.\n\n## 1. Session Lifecycle & Management\n\nTo support a multi-user web environment, the backend must manage `AgentSession` instances as stateful services.\n\n### Session Store\n\n- **Mapping**: Implement a `Map<SessionId, AgentSessionRuntime>` on the server.\n- **Persistence**: Leverage `SessionManager.open(sessionPath)` to resume sessions from the `.jsonl` files.\n- **Resource Isolation**: Each session must have its own `cwd` and `AgentDir` to avoid cross-session file contamination.\n\n### Lifecycle Management\n\n- **Startup**: Use `createAgentSession()` to initialize the runtime.\n- **Teardown**: Call `runtime.dispose()` and `session.dispose()` when a user disconnects or a session is closed to kill orphaned bash processes and save state.\n===== PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md =====\n# Portable Deployment Guide\n\nCold-start KainBain on a machine that has never seen it — no homelab\nservices, no uncommitted notes, no author on call. This repo runs its suites on a shared 4-core host under the\noverlapped gate (`npm test` runs api + frontend + lint + build + scans in one\nwindow), so a green run on an idle box is not evidence of stability. The\nstandard here is **a pass rate**, measured by repeating the suite.\n\n## Measuring a flake\n\n`scripts/repeat-tests.mjs` runs one suite (optionally filtered to one file)\n`N` times and prints the per-run result plus the pass rate. Every run appends a\nJSON object to a JSONL log under the OS temp dir and keeps the raw suite output\nbeside it, so a failing run's exact signature can be read afterwards.\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite api      --pattern api/index.test.js --runs 10\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite frontend --pattern StageSkillsPanel   --runs 10\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite canary   --runs 3\n```\n===== agent-docs/GATE_PROGRESS_AND_HEARTBEATS.md =====\n# Long quiet steps must emit progress (gate author rule)\n\n> Rule of thumb: **any step that can be silent for more than ~60 seconds must\n> emit progress or a heartbeat.** Silence is not liveness — to the engine, to\n> the operator, and to the stall watchdog.\n\nThe engine's CI/script stall watchdog is a *silence* guard with a\nlast-resort role (`KAINBAIN_CI_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 5 min): a running\ncommand stage heartbeats on the\n`KAINBAIN_CI_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS` keep-alive (default 30s) while its child\nis alive, so a quiet-but-healthy stage survives by design. That means a\n**wedged** stage is now bounded by the stage `timeout` and the gate's own\nbranch budgets — not by the watchdog. This requires a robust JS middleware to manage long-running agent sessions, stream real-time events, and handle non-linear conversation trees.\n\n## 1. Session Lifecycle & Management\n\nTo support a multi-user web environment, the backend must manage `AgentSession` instances as stateful services.\n\n### Session Store\n\n- **Mapping**: Implement a `Map<SessionId, AgentSessionRuntime>` on the server.\n- **Persistence**: Leverage `SessionManager.open(sessionPath)` to resume sessions from the `.jsonl` files.\n- **Resource Isolation**: Each session must have its own `cwd` and `AgentDir` to avoid cross-session file contamination.\n\n### Lifecycle Management\n\n- **Startup**: Use `createAgentSession()` to initialize the runtime.\n- **Teardown**: Call `runtime.dispose()` and `session.dispose()` when a user disconnects or a session is closed to kill orphaned bash processes and save state.\n===== PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md =====\n# Portable Deployment Guide\n\nCold-start KainBain on a machine that has never seen it — no homelab\nservices, no uncommitted notes, no author on call. This repo runs its suites on a shared 4-core host under the\noverlapped gate (`npm test` runs api + frontend + lint + build + scans in one\nwindow), so a green run on an idle box is not evidence of stability. The\nstandard here is **a pass rate**, measured by repeating the suite.\n\n## Measuring a flake\n\n`scripts/repeat-tests.mjs` runs one suite (optionally filtered to one file)\n`N` times and prints the per-run result plus the pass rate. Every run appends a\nJSON object to a JSONL log under the OS temp dir and keeps the raw suite output\nbeside it, so a failing run's exact signature can be read afterwards.\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite api      --pattern api/index.test.js --runs 10\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite frontend --pattern StageSkillsPanel   --runs 10\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite canary   --runs 3\n```\n===== agent-docs/GATE_PROGRESS_AND_HEARTBEATS.md =====\n# Long quiet steps must emit progress (gate author rule)\n\n> Rule of thumb: **any step that can be silent for more than ~60 seconds must\n> emit progress or a heartbeat.** Silence is not liveness — to the engine, to\n> the operator, and to the stall watchdog.\n\nThe engine's CI/script stall watchdog is a *silence* guard with a\nlast-resort role (`KAINBAIN_CI_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 5 min): a running\ncommand stage heartbeats on the\n`KAINBAIN_CI_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS` keep-alive (default 30s) while its child\nis alive, so a quiet-but-healthy stage survives by design. That means a\n**wedged** stage is now bounded by the stage `timeout` and the gate's own\nbranch budgets — not by the watchdog. If you author or modify a gate,\nrepeat-runner, or long command, keep the following contract so the next\nquiet step never recreates the October 2026 false-stall incident\n(task `cafbf7b8`, root cause + plan in\n`docs/tasks/cafbf7b8-c3c4-489e-909c-20d2698bfe65/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`).\n\n## Contract for gate authors\n\n===== agent-docs/GitGuidance.md =====\n# Git Guidance for Agents\n\n> **Status:** initial version created for AUDIT R2 (forward pointer from\n> `agents.md`). Current State Analysis\n\nThe application currently has:\n\n- **Backend**: Fastify API with WebSocket event bridge, project/task/workflow stores, and integration with the PI Agent SDK.\n- **Frontend**: React-based UI with context-driven state, real-time event streaming, and a workflow canvas/kanban board.\n- **Core Loop**: Users can create projects, define workflow stages, submit tasks, and observe the agent executing them via streaming events.\n\n## 2. Reliability & Stability (The \"No-Crash\" Goal)\n\nThe app currently lacks robust error handling and session persistence.\n\n- **Session Persistence**: Sessions are currently in-memory. This requires a robust JS middleware to manage long-running agent sessions, stream real-time events, and handle non-linear conversation trees.\n\n## 1. Session Lifecycle & Management\n\nTo support a multi-user web environment, the backend must manage `AgentSession` instances as stateful services.\n\n### Session Store\n\n- **Mapping**: Implement a `Map<SessionId, AgentSessionRuntime>` on the server.\n- **Persistence**: Leverage `SessionManager.open(sessionPath)` to resume sessions from the `.jsonl` files.\n- **Resource Isolation**: Each session must have its own `cwd` and `AgentDir` to avoid cross-session file contamination.\n\n### Lifecycle Management\n\n- **Startup**: Use `createAgentSession()` to initialize the runtime.\n- **Teardown**: Call `runtime.dispose()` and `session.dispose()` when a user disconnects or a session is closed to kill orphaned bash processes and save state.\n===== PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md =====\n# Portable Deployment Guide\n\nCold-start KainBain on a machine that has never seen it — no homelab\nservices, no uncommitted notes, no author on call. This repo runs its suites on a shared 4-core host under the\noverlapped gate (`npm test` runs api + frontend + lint + build + scans in one\nwindow), so a green run on an idle box is not evidence of stability. The\nstandard here is **a pass rate**, measured by repeating the suite.\n\n## Measuring a flake\n\n`scripts/repeat-tests.mjs` runs one suite (optionally filtered to one file)\n`N` times and prints the per-run result plus the pass rate. Every run appends a\nJSON object to a JSONL log under the OS temp dir and keeps the raw suite output\nbeside it, so a failing run's exact signature can be read afterwards.\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite api      --pattern api/index.test.js --runs 10\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite frontend --pattern StageSkillsPanel   --runs 10\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite canary   --runs 3\n```\n===== agent-docs/GATE_PROGRESS_AND_HEARTBEATS.md =====\n# Long quiet steps must emit progress (gate author rule)\n\n> Rule of thumb: **any step that can be silent for more than ~60 seconds must\n> emit progress or a heartbeat.** Silence is not liveness — to the engine, to\n> the operator, and to the stall watchdog.\n\nThe engine's CI/script stall watchdog is a *silence* guard with a\nlast-resort role (`KAINBAIN_CI_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 5 min): a running\ncommand stage heartbeats on the\n`KAINBAIN_CI_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS` keep-alive (default 30s) while its child\nis alive, so a quiet-but-healthy stage survives by design. That means a\n**wedged** stage is now bounded by the stage `timeout` and the gate's own\nbranch budgets — not by the watchdog. If you author or modify a gate,\nrepeat-runner, or long command, keep the following contract so the next\nquiet step never recreates the October 2026 false-stall incident\n(task `cafbf7b8`, root cause + plan in\n`docs/tasks/cafbf7b8-c3c4-489e-909c-20d2698bfe65/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`).\n\n## Contract for gate authors\n\n===== agent-docs/GitGuidance.md =====\n# Git Guidance for Agents\n\n> **Status:** initial version created for AUDIT R2 (forward pointer from\n> `agents.md`). The goal is to move from \"feature-complete but fragile\" to \"stable enough for real-world usage.\"\n\n## 1. Current State Analysis\n\nThe application currently has:\n\n- **Backend**: Fastify API with WebSocket event bridge, project/task/workflow stores, and integration with the PI Agent SDK.\n- **Frontend**: React-based UI with context-driven state, real-time event streaming, and a workflow canvas/kanban board.\n- **Core Loop**: Users can create projects, define workflow stages, submit tasks, and observe the agent executing them via streaming events.\n\n## 2. Critical Gaps for Dogfooding\n\n### A. Reliability & Stability (The \"No-Crash\" Goal)\n\nThe app currently lacks robust error handling and session persistence.\n\n- **Session Persistence**: Sessions are currently in-memory. If the server restarts, all active sessions are lost.\n- **Error Recovery**: WebSocket disconnects trigger reconnection, but there's no \"sync\" mechanism to recover missed events during the gap.\n===== phase2_plan.md =====\n# Phase 2: PI Agent UI Integration Plan\n\n## Overview\n\nThe goal is to build a high-performance UI layer over the PI AI Agent, transforming it from a CLI-centric tool into a fully interactive web application. This requires a robust JS middleware to manage long-running agent sessions, stream real-time events, and handle non-linear conversation trees.\n\n## 1. Session Lifecycle & Management\n\nTo support a multi-user web environment, the backend must manage `AgentSession` instances as stateful services.\n\n### Session Store\n\n- **Mapping**: Implement a `Map<SessionId, AgentSessionRuntime>` on the server.\n- **Persistence**: Leverage `SessionManager.open(sessionPath)` to resume sessions from the `.jsonl` files.\n- **Resource Isolation**: Each session must have its own `cwd` and `AgentDir` to avoid cross-session file contamination.\n\n### Lifecycle Management\n\n- **Startup**: Use `createAgentSession()` to initialize the runtime.\n- **Teardown**: Call `runtime.dispose()` and `session.dispose()` when a user disconnects or a session is closed to kill orphaned bash processes and save state.\n===== PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md =====\n# Portable Deployment Guide\n\nCold-start KainBain on a machine that has never seen it — no homelab\nservices, no uncommitted notes, no author on call. This repo runs its suites on a shared 4-core host under the\noverlapped gate (`npm test` runs api + frontend + lint + build + scans in one\nwindow), so a green run on an idle box is not evidence of stability. The\nstandard here is **a pass rate**, measured by repeating the suite.\n\n## Measuring a flake\n\n`scripts/repeat-tests.mjs` runs one suite (optionally filtered to one file)\n`N` times and prints the per-run result plus the pass rate. Every run appends a\nJSON object to a JSONL log under the OS temp dir and keeps the raw suite output\nbeside it, so a failing run's exact signature can be read afterwards.\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite api      --pattern api/index.test.js --runs 10\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite frontend --pattern StageSkillsPanel   --runs 10\nnode scripts/repeat-tests.mjs --suite canary   --runs 3\n```\n===== agent-docs/GATE_PROGRESS_AND_HEARTBEATS.md =====\n# Long quiet steps must emit progress (gate author rule)\n\n> Rule of thumb: **any step that can be silent for more than ~60 seconds must\n> emit progress or a heartbeat.** Silence is not liveness — to the engine, to\n> the operator, and to the stall watchdog.\n\nThe engine's CI/script stall watchdog is a *silence* guard with a\nlast-resort role (`KAINBAIN_CI_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 5 min): a running\ncommand stage heartbeats on the\n`KAINBAIN_CI_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS` keep-alive (default 30s) while its child\nis alive, so a quiet-but-healthy stage survives by design. That means a\n**wedged** stage is now bounded by the stage `timeout` and the gate's own\nbranch budgets — not by the watchdog. If you author or modify a gate,\nrepeat-runner, or long command, keep the following contract so the next\nquiet step never recreates the October 2026 false-stall incident\n(task `cafbf7b8`, root cause + plan in\n`docs/tasks/cafbf7b8-c3c4-489e-909c-20d2698bfe65/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`).\n\n## Contract for gate authors\n\n===== agent-docs/GitGuidance.md =====\n# Git Guidance for Agents\n\n> **Status:** initial version created for AUDIT R2 (forward pointer from\n> `agents.md`). Start with frontmatter — all four fields required:\n\n```md\n---\ntitle: My Article\nsection: how-it-works\norder: 10\nslug: my-article\n---\n\n# My Article\n...\n```\n\n3. Make-change-easy safeguards\n\n- One owner/branch touch per phase: no parallel writes to the same root or scanner file.\n- `git mv` to preserve rename detection.\n- Small, separately understandable commits or at least separate command steps: inventory baseline → moves → deletions → link updates → verification. Largely a higher number (or step with the ladder analogue) should only be pursued if the earlier stages have been attempted and failed. \n\n## Priority & Goal\n\nThe main goal is:\n\n- To Prevent/Limit Human intervention needed\n- To prevent burn out of token usage limits.\n\nSome other important,although less so, goals are:\n\n- To prevent misaligned behaviour\n- To prevent wasted compute and energy\n- To maintain network security\n\n## Escalation ladder\n\nIn summary it is:\n\n1) Automated Scripted in task recovery\n2) Agent lead in task recovery\n3) Task interrupt and resume\n4) Task retry from current stage with existing branch\n5) Fail the task, to allow earlier stages to correct issues.\n6) Request for Human intervention, Continue standard operations\n7) Halt task until Human intervention, continue with others\n8) Halt all tasks, Restart the app/redeploy\n9) Halt all tasks, wait for human intevention\n\n\n### Step 1 Automated scripted in task recovery\n\n#### Description\n\nThis means issues are handled naturally in code. This can be things such as retry loops, backup implementations and general reliable design. This is the cheapest,easiest and safest method of recovery and the key to this is it is handled without using tokens, this barely seeming any different to the app just working as intended.\n\n#### Examples\n\n- API backoff retry loops\n- try catch handling of errors\n- Minimal data transformation\n- Preventative design\n- Force shutdowns if things cant be done properly\n\n### Step 2 Agent lead in task recovery\n\n#### Description\n\nThis largely if there is an error while an agent is running, hoping it surfaces mid run and therefore they can solve it. Again shouldnt look any different to a user to normal operations, just maybe some different logs or higher token output\n\n#### Examples\n\n- Failing tests\n- Verdict requirements\n- Files being in different places than usual.\n  \n### Step 3 Task interrupt and resume\n\n#### Description\n\nThis is the “turn it off and on again” part of a task. Hopefully things can be resumed middle of the task with little interactions. The only thing the user should notice is it taking a little longer than usual. \n\n#### Examples\n\n- Finishing merge after interruption\n- Recovering after a restart/deploy\n- Session resume on connectivity issues to agents\n- User pauses and unpauses the operation\n\n### Step 4 Task retry from current stage with existing branch\n\n#### Description \nThis is where we effectively do the stage from scratch. Uses when we think the current stage is unrecoverable. This is essentially treating it as a new task entering a stage. \n\n##### examples\n\n- retry stage as an agent triggered loop protection\n- connection issues caused the agent to fail so retry\n- Error processing approval on a human stage\n\n### step 5 Fail the task, to allow earlier stages to correct issues\n\n#### Description \nThis is failing to a previous stage in a hope thatll fix it. There is always a risk this causes loops and it is depending on the users configuration a lot. \n\n\n#### Examples\n- merge conflict on merge stage failing back to an agent stage to resolve.\n- system test stage fails back to an agent to fix\n- a agent stage has failed multiple times and falls back to a human review.\n\n\n### Step 6 Request for Human intervention, Continue standard operations\n\n#### Description \nThis is where we alert the user and provide an option to intervene while still trying the earlier methods. This is different to just good Observability on this behaviour as it is specifically requesting that human intervention is likely needed, but we still keep trying. \n\n\n#### Examples\n- nearing a retry notification limit we may flag it as problematic\n- Early notice of a possible loop\n- having a temporary freeze option for a user to intervene as needed (while still running if not )\n- push notification to user for multiple failing tasks\n- flag that an alias model or harness reliability goes below a threshold (over enough samples)\n\n### Step 7 Halt task until Human intervention, continue with others\n\n#### Description \nAll tasks should be isolated from eachother so in most cases even if one task is borked we can let it continue to operate others. This will need to be flagged to the user to come intervene and provide tools and any information needed. This generally should be avoided as is a clear sign the project is stuck\n\n#### Examples\n\n- Retry loop exhaustion, Escalating from earlier warnings\n- Some wierd git behaviour that cant be resolved automatically and needs manual resoloution\n- Model choice is causing all tasks on a stage to fail constantly and require user to fix harness/model\n- Unable to find referenced files that where assumed existing and it would be unsafe/illogical to create them now or procede without\n\n\n### Step 8 Halt all tasks, Restart the app/redeploy\n\n#### Description\nThis is to tackle system wide issues and almost never should be pulled, however is the ultimate turn it off and on again. This involves restarting kainbain and making sure it is on the latest version. \n\n#### Examples\n- Unable to run any exec or terminal access commands to restart to pickup changes\n- Error during redeployment needing a fresh redeploy(or revert and deploy)\n- UI requests are entirely unable to reach the backend\n- Missing core file requiring a restart to guarentee file is accesible\n\n\n### Step 9 Halt Everything wait for human intervention\n\n#### Description\n\nAt the end of the day some things will need a human to fix them, this therefore involves making sure all the knowledge and reasons why things failed are availble for the user to come and fix it. It is also involving purposely not doing anything so that the user doesnt have to contend with moving behavuoir while trying to fix it (Like you’d turn an engine off before working on it)\n\n#### Examples\n\n- App Restart exhaustion\n- Deploy retry exhaustion\n- Severe/repeated guard mechanisms tripping\n- Deployment server in repeated restart loop\n\n\n## Observability vs request for help\n\nIt is important to note that we always want to maintain observability of when remediation steps are taken and this should be reflected. A request for help should be noticably different and actively raise concerns to the user. For example we may log early steps to the logs so we can see whats happened, where as if we need user support we may have a popup on the screen. \n\n\n#project/kainbain #risk #documentation #esclationLadder #response \n\n\n{\n  \"chunk_id\": \"exec-2-1\",\n  \"command\": \"ls \\\"docs/Reliability&Risk/RiskRegister/\\\" 2>&1; echo \\\"===\\\"; cat \\\"docs/Reliability&Risk/EscalationLadder.md\\\" 2>&1 | head -n 200\",\n  \"description\": \"List risk register contents\",\n  \"exit_code\": 0,\n  \"terminal_status\": \"completed\",\n  \"output\": \"Agent-Connection-Drops.md\\nTemplate.md\\nUI-Workflow-Notice-Banner-Removal.md\\n===\\n# Escalation ladder\\n\\nThis indicates the order of how abnormal or possibly disruptive events should be handled. This is the cheapest,easiest and safest method of recovery and the key to this is it is handled without using tokens, this barely seeming any different to the app just working as intended.\\n\\n#### Examples\\n\\n- API backoff retry loops\\n- try catch handling of errors\\n- Minimal data transformation\\n- Preventative design\\n- Force shutdowns if things cant be done properly\\n\\n### Step 2 Agent lead in task recovery\\n\\n#### Description\\n\\nThis largely if there is an error while an agent is running, hoping it surfaces mid run and therefore they can solve it.
